deities: Lord Shiva as Jalpeshwar (Ananta Shiva Linga, worshipped in a basement sanctum about 11 ft below ground, reached by touch rather than sight)
festivals: Shravani Mela (July-August, Shravan; Kanwariya yatra with devotees chanting 'Bholey Bom')

history.dynasty: Cooch Behar (Koch dynasty): founded 1524 by Bishwa Singha (father of Maharaja Nara Narayan), rebuilt 1563, rebuilt 1663 by Maharaja Pran Narayan; under Raikats of Baikunthapur from 1621 after Mahidev Raikut broke from the Koch dynasty; restored 30 January 1899 by Rani Jagadeswari Devi (wife of Raja Jagendra Deva Raikut) after an 1897 earthquake
history.period: Present structure 1524-1663; legend traces the shrine to ~800 AD (Jalpesh, descendant of King Bhagadatta of Kamrup) - weakly sourced
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: this temple is at Jalpesh village, ~7 km from Maynaguri town, NOT in Jalpaiguri town (Jalpaiguri town is ~23 km away). Documented with the corrected location. One of North Bengal's most important Shiva shrines, on the banks of the Jarda river in the Dooars. Legend: the Ananta Shiva Linga lies in a basement garbha griha about 11 ft below ground, kept partly under water - devotees touch rather than see it (crowd restrictions were ordered by Calcutta High Court in August 2022 during Shravan). Earlier history is legendary: an ~800 AD founding by Jalpesh of Kamrup, destruction during Bakhtiyar Khalji's invasion (~1200), a Bhutanese-king rebuild in the 12th century, and abandonment before the Koch rebuilds. The 2015 Jalpaiguri earthquake (26 April 2015) cracked the temple's walls and spire.

name: Jalpesh Temple
town: Jalpesh, Maynaguri block (CSV town 'Jalpaiguri' is WRONG - temple is ~7 km from Maynaguri town)
town_description: Maynaguri is a market town in Jalpaiguri district in the Dooars foothills, about 23 km northeast of Jalpaiguri town. It is a local trade and transport hub and the gateway to the Jalpesh and Jatileshwar temples; the Teen Bigha corridor to Bangladesh lies nearby. The surrounding plain is agricultural with tea gardens on the fringes.

travel.railway: Jalpaiguri station - about 23 km; Maynaguri station about 6 km from the temple.
travel.road: 6 km from Maynaguri, 23 km from Jalpaiguri town; good roads (NH-31D corridor); taxis, buses, auto-rickshaws and van rickshaws.

visitor_information.best_time: July-August (Shravan) for the Shravani Mela and Kanwariya yatra; February-March for Maha Shivaratri; November-February for a peaceful visit.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: 7:00 AM-7:00 PM (map listing), 6:00 AM-8:00 PM (velpu.com), 24 hours (Justdial) - verify. Expect crowd controls around the basement sanctum in Shravan.
